capabilities: Expose full CRUD on vault files over an authenticated HTTPS REST API
Patch targeted note sections (headings, blocks, frontmatter) without rewriting whole files
Serve a built-in MCP server so AI agents can read, write, search, and run commands
Stream vault events as Server-Sent Events with JsonLogic filters
Let other plugins register custom routes, MCP tools, and events via an extension API
extras: Extensive security hardening: configuration-directory access blocked by default (CVE/GHSA-documented), failed authentication throttled, locally generated CA certificate. The header-based PATCH targeting format is deprecated and will be removed in version 6.0.
intentEvidence: Inspired by Vinzent03's advanced-uri plugin, with the goal of expanding automation options beyond the constraints of custom URL schemes.
motivation: The author was inspired by Vinzent03's advanced-uri plugin and wanted automation options beyond the constraints of custom URL schemes.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way for outside programs or AI agents to programmatically read and modify vault notes.

relations.evidence: Inspired by Vinzent03's advanced-uri plugin, with the goal of expanding automation options beyond the constraints of custom URL schemes.
Several third-party MCP servers for Obsidian exist, but they are no longer necessary
Periodic Notes: Adds support for periodic notes

requires.name: MCP client (e.g. Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor)

summary: REST API and MCP server that lets external scripts, browser extensions, and AI agents read, search, and edit notes in the vault.
